entries.name: cuisine
entries.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset for a French real estate photo demonstration gallery. ONE wide 3:1 diptych, divided exactly at the midpoint into two equal 3:2 photographic panels, no gutter, no divider, no text. LEFT is BEFORE, RIGHT is AFTER. Both panels show EXACTLY the SAME room, locked camera position, identical perspective and architectural geometry, 28mm interior photo. Real attainable apartments, natural imperfect surfaces, nuanced daylight and shadows, authentic photographic texture. NO 3D render, NO excessive HDR, NO glossy showroom styling, no people, text, captions, watermarks or collage borders. Keep architecture, doors, windows, built-ins, sockets and outdoor view identical across the two panels. A modest long kitchen in a 1990s French apartment: off-white cabinets, terracotta square floor tiles, laminate oak worktop, tiled splashback, right end window, stainless sink. BEFORE: dull underexposed daylight, dishes drying by sink, a grocery bag, tea towels and cereal package on worktop. AFTER: exposure and white balance corrected to fresh natural daylight, clearer shadows, clutter removed, ONE folded towel remains. Exactly same cabinets, counters, stools and perspective. No new styling objects. Realistic grain and reflections. Improve light and tidy only.

entries.name: salon-refait
entries.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: fictional before-and-after examples for a French real estate photo studio website. Generate ONE photographic comparison sheet without text, labels, borders, gutters or watermarks. Total canvas ratio exactly 3:1 landscape, panels of equal width seamlessly side by side. Same fixed tripod eye level, identical lens, angle, crop and physical room in every panel; no camera drift. All load-bearing walls, ceiling shape, door openings, windows, radiators, sockets and fixed plumbing must stay EXACTLY in the same positions, dimensions, colours, shapes in every panel. Changes only to explicitly requested finishes and movable furniture. Deeply realistic real estate photography, natural window light, subtle wood grain, cloth creases, imperfect plaster, believable shadows. No CGI, glossy render, HDR, extra windows, enlarged room or impossible furniture. The transformation must be noticeable and desirable, an attractive tasteful real home rather than a sterile showroom.
Composition: THREE square panels in one horizontal row: BEFORE, FIRST PROPOSAL, FINAL CORRECTION, from left to right. Full room visible in all.
A modest 22m2 rectangular French living room. One tall white double casement window on BACK wall slightly left of centre with a white cast iron radiator directly below it. One open door in the RIGHT wall near the back reveals a dark corridor. Keep window, radiator and door absolutely identical in every panel, same dimensions and visibility. White ceiling.
LEFT: outdated room with worn beige small square floor tiles, pale yellow walls, a brown bulky leather sofa against LEFT wall, dated dark bulky coffee table, mismatched media cabinet low along right wall before doorway. Restrained clutter, not filthy.
MIDDLE: transform dramatically: pale natural oak herringbone floor replacing tiles, warm ivory painted walls, modern pale cream fabric sofa on left, a large softly curved walnut coffee table, textured off-white rug, elegant low oak cabinet on right, linen sheer curtains beside but not hiding radiator, subtle art above sofa, small olive green cushions. Stylish and genuinely lived in. Same room, no structural changes.
RIGHT: maintain EXACTLY the middle panel oak floor, ivory walls, sofa, cabinet, curtains, art and lighting, change ONLY walnut coffee table to a compact ROUND travertine table and olive cushions to burnt-orange cushions. Everything else locked. This explicitly illustrates a focused correction after a complete first redesign. No added table/cushion duplication. Strong before-after differentiation.

entries.name: amenagement-angle
entries.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Use ONLY the RIGHT furnished-room panel of the reference comparison sheet as the scene. Produce ONE single landscape 3:2 photograph, not a diptych. Show the same finished room from a gently different viewpoint: camera translated about 40 cm toward the right and rotated slightly left towards the navy sofa. Stay within the already documented visible surfaces. Keep EXACTLY the same two tall white windows in the rear wall, the white cast-iron radiator BETWEEN them, door opening on the right wall, white mouldings, parquet direction, ceiling and wall geometry. Do not add, move, cover or remove any window, door, radiator. Keep all finished-room furniture and decor identical: navy sofa along left wall, oval walnut low table with books and vase, cream rug, round dining table with TWO wood chairs near right rear window, slender brass floor lamp beside sofa, existing framed print, plants. No newly revealed extra space or invented opening. The same room must be unmistakably recognizable; only camera perspective changes, NOT the design. Natural honest real estate photography with realistic soft daylight, no CGI gloss, no overly wide lens, no labels or text. Preserve actual room dimensions.
